new_candidates.source: landscape-sweep-20260926: Layer alternatives list (conditional), plus the open-gap analysis, a GitHub GraphQL/REST changelog read and the official Claude Code/Agent SDK docs
new_candidates.demonstrated_gap: Open gap 5 (independent-host recovery and power-loss durability unqualified) has no built-in native answer on the Claude side. The official sessions doc says session files stay on the machine that created them and plain resume works on that machine only. The first-party Python SDK adds an operator-owned SessionStore (0.1.64, with a 13-contract conformance harness and reference S3/Redis/Postgres adapters). Its session_store_flush='eager' option is documented for cross-process resume and crash durability (0.1.73), and it adds resume_drops_turn/resume_session_at guards (0.2.137), in-process @tool MCP servers and hook callbacks. It still runs the unmodified bundled Claude Code (0.2.160 bundles CLI 2.1.283). Anthropic's legal page lets an end user sign in to the unmodified binary with their own subscription, and the help center describes Agent SDK use on Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise plan credentials, so the same-account check is feasible. The same trial also yields the first macos-arm64 evidence; both winners are untested there.
new_candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Use one frozen bounded research task with the same native claude login (no API key), model and effort on the WSL workstation and a Mac. Arm A (native): claude -p --output-format stream-json --session-id on WSL, SIGKILL mid-tool-call, copy the JSONL to the Mac and run claude --resume there. Arm B (SDK 0.2.160): the same task with a self-hosted reference Redis or Postgres SessionStore on the workstation (passing run_session_store_conformance), session_store_flush='eager', SIGKILL mid-turn, then resume from the store on the Mac with the same cwd. Adopt B only if it matches A on account identity and plan-usage attribution, exactly-once external effects, transcript completeness up to the kill and cache-read/token totals, and loses less state at the kill point. Keep native if copying the file recovers the same state, or if B needs an API key or any other non-native credential.

new_candidates.demonstrated_gap: This layer has no gap for it today. It is the Claude counterpart to codex-acp, which is already conditional for ACP hosts such as DeerFlow. Source read of Cisco skill-scanner (HEAD 4f8bec34; release 2.1.0, 2026-09-05):

Codex rust-v0.157.0 (2026-09-25) turns subagents on by default. It sets model and reasoning effort per agent, caps concurrency with an [agents] setting, returns snapshots from close_agent (#47252) and cleans up cancelled child agents (#47348). In non-interactive flows it passes failures that need approval back to the parent. These map directly onto the layer's cancellation and preserved-failure checks. The trial needs no new credential: it uses the native ChatGPT sign-in, and the stack already pins 0.155.1. new_candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Use the frozen coding/research task with fixed acceptance commands. Arm A: Codex 0.157.x subagents with custom agent files, agents.max_concurrent_threads_per_session set, and default_subagent_model and default_subagent_reasoning_effort matched to the task. Arm B: a Claude Code >=2.1.283 Workflow with isolation: worktree routed through Worktrunk hooks. Score each arm on (1) independent acceptance pass; (2) stopping mid-run leaves no orphan child threads or edits; (3) each child's writes stay inside the worktree it owns, and colliding writes to a shared tree count as a fail; (4) a failed child's result reaches the parent verbatim; (5) returned usage reconciles with the provider counters. If Codex matches acceptance and passes ownership and cancellation with complete usage, it becomes a co-equal worker lane. If it fails ownership, it stays a single-worker or reviewer lane.

new_candidates.source: landscape-sweep-20260926: Survivor from sweep_20260923. Re-checked through GitHub GraphQL/REST (releases, README, license endpoint), the OmniDocBench README leaderboard and Hugging Face model API.
new_candidates.demonstrated_gap: The winners leave OCR, inferred layouts, arbitrary filings and MarkItDown's PDF/Office extras unqualified. Poppler acceptance covers only designed born-digital Latin pages. MinerU 4.0 (4.0.0 released 2026-09-16, 4.0.7 on 2026-09-23) is a local-first agent CLI. It parses PDFs, scans, DOC/DOCX, PPT/PPTX, XLS/XLSX, HTML/MHTML, EPUB and CSV in four tiers (flash, basic, standard, advanced) and keeps a local document library with `mineru find`/`search`. `mineru read` returns stable citation locators (doc:{id}/tier/page/block) plus page or block images, so an agent can re-read the original page or block before relying on a hit. That is this layer's read-the-original contract, which qmd+Poppler meets only for text. Default install: ONNX CPU small models plus a llama.cpp VLM. mineru[full] targets NVIDIA, and the default package is already the recommended one on macOS. Documents go remote only with an explicit --remote, and a local failure never falls back to remote. Measured: MinerU2.5-Pro-2605-1.2B (Apache-2.0 weights) scores 95.75 on OmniDocBench v1.6, a benchmark authored by the same lab (bias flagged). A competitor-run olmOCR-bench gives the MinerU pipeline 72.7 overall and 83.3 on born-digital pages. Flags: the code license is Apache-2.0 plus extra terms (a commercial licence is needed above 100M MAU or USD 20M monthly revenue; online services must give attribution; the licence terminates automatically on breach). Telemetry uploads stop only when explicitly disabled. The library needs a `mineru server` process to be managed. Patches ship at a high rate (8 releases in 8 days), so any trial pins an exact patch.
new_candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Build a sealed corpus with hand-checked ground truth and judged queries: born-digital filings and exhibits, difficult-layout decks and tables, scanned pages and Office files. Compare MinerU basic and standard tiers (telemetry off, no --remote, mineru[full] on the RTX 4090; macOS default package on the M5 Pro) with Poppler pdftotext for PDFs and MarkItDown 0.1.8 for HTML/Office. Measure text edit distance, table TEDS, reading-order edit and exact-phrase locator round-trip to the original page. Measure `mineru search`+`read` against qmd lex/hybrid on recall@5 and nDCG@10, with repeated cold and warm latency. Adopt MinerU as the difficult-layout/OCR parser only if it materially reduces errors on non-born-digital pages without regressing born-digital exactness or locator round-trips. Reject it if gains are within run-to-run variance.

new_candidates.source: landscape-sweep-20260926: Seeded candidate: 'ColPali / vidore-benchmark', the coordinator's P1 trial. Verified through GitHub GraphQL/README, the arXiv abstract and the Hugging Face API. WebSearch was used for the ViDoRe V3 leaderboard.
new_candidates.demonstrated_gap: qmd retrieves only over extracted text. Pages whose evidence is in charts, image tables or scans (earnings decks, annual-report tables) have little or no text layer, so BM25 and text vectors cannot reach them. The layer's open gaps state that representative-corpus recall is unestablished and OCR and inferred layouts are unqualified. ViDoRe V3 (arXiv 2601.08620, revised 2026-04-21) reports that visual retrievers outperform textual ones, and that late-interaction models and textual reranking substantially improve retrieval. It includes a human-judged financial split, vidore/vidore_v3_finance_en (CC-BY-4.0). colpali-engine v0.3.18 (2026-08-22, MIT) runs Apache-2.0 ColQwen3 checkpoints locally on CUDA or MPS. tomoro-colqwen3-embed-4b (base Qwen3-VL-4B, Apache-2.0) scores 90.6 and colqwen3.5-4.5B-v3 90.9 in the README's ViDoRe table. The retrieved unit is the original page image, which can be paired with Poppler text of the same page to meet the read-original contract. The vidore-benchmark pipeline evaluator accepts arbitrary custom pipelines, so the same judged queries can score qmd's text pipeline too. That supplies part of the relevance-judged corpus the layer's next_action asks for.
new_candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Use the vidore-benchmark pipeline evaluator (custom BasePipeline) on vidore_v3_finance_en (English) plus our own sealed difficult-page subset. Compare (a) the dataset's page text, or Poppler text, fed to qmd lex and hybrid; (b) ColQwen3-4B through colpali-engine; (c) RRF fusion of (a) and (b). Measure nDCG@10 and recall@5 plus indexing and search time on the RTX 4090, with an MPS run on the M5 Pro. Adopt visual or fused retrieval as a complement to qmd only if it beats the text pipeline by a material margin on both the public finance split and our subset at acceptable index cost. Otherwise keep text-only qmd.

new_candidates.demonstrated_gap: Seeded (coordinator P2). No gap for this requirement. HippoRAG 2 is a document-memory framework whose indexing runs LLM OpenIE extraction over every passage. Its API takes an llm_model_name alongside the embedding model, and its reproduction uses gpt-4o-mini or Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct OpenIE, with an offline vLLM example spread over 4 GPUs. new_candidates.source: landscape-sweep-20260926: A WebSearch for the seeded PyLate/ColBERT late-interaction item found LightOn's ColGREP (next-plaid). Verified with GitHub GraphQL (repository, README, colgrep/README and release reads), the HF blog and the HF model API.
new_candidates.demonstrated_gap: On the layer's sealed 35-question agent-lab set, the winning pipeline (SocratiCode 1.14.0 + Qdrant + Nemotron-3-Embed-1B on vLLM) scored Recall@5 0.857 / MRR 0.721. The same embedder queried directly scored 0.971 / 0.853, so the loss comes from the indexing and ranking pipeline, not the model. SocratiCode's index/watcher recovery is not_established, and all three winners are untested on macos-arm64. ColGREP, the tool in this repository, replaces the three services with one local Rust binary: no server, no Qdrant, no embedding service. It checks for changed files and updates its index on every search, so there is no watcher daemon to recover. It keeps one index per (project, model) and fuses ColBERT MaxSim with FTS5 trigram keyword search by RRF. It ships macOS arm64 binaries with CoreML/Accelerate. Its default models are the Apache-2.0 late-interaction code retrievers LateOn-Code-edge (17M) and LateOn-Code, both trained with PyLate; this row carries the seeded PyLate/ColBERT item. The encoder runs in-process rather than as a service. The layer's overturn clause is outcome-based (sealed-set quality plus latency, memory and lifecycle), so a service-free index qualifies if it wins.

new_candidates.source: landscape-sweep-20260926: Found through the ColGREP README, which benchmarks against Semble's public bench. Confirmed with a WebSearch and GitHub GraphQL reads of the repository, README, benchmarks/README and release notes.
new_candidates.demonstrated_gap: Same pipeline and platform gaps as above: SocratiCode 0.857/0.721 against the incumbent embedder's own 0.971/0.853 on the sealed set; watcher recovery not_established; winners untested on macos-arm64. Semble is an MIT library, CLI and MCP server that runs on CPU with no GPU, API key, embedding service or vector database. It combines potion-code-16M-v2 static embeddings (MIT), BM25 and a ranking stage. Its per-repo index is cached in the OS cache folder and invalidated automatically when files change, so recovery means a fast rebuild instead of a watcher and Qdrant restore. Its public pinned benchmark (1,251 queries, 63 repos, 19 languages) reports NDCG@10 of 0.854, against CodeRankEmbed 0.839, ColGREP 0.693, BM25 0.673 and codebase-memory-mcp 0.630. In its ablation the ranking stage adds about 0.16 to 0.17 NDCG. SocratiCode has no such stage: its README documents only dense + BM25 RRF. SocratiCode and the Nemotron embedder were never measured on that benchmark.
new_candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Install semble 0.6.1 with `uv tool install` in an isolated prefix. Configure its MCP entry by hand rather than with `semble install`, which also writes AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md instructions and a sub-agent. Use local paths only. Run it with content set to code and docs on the sealed 35-question set and on a fresh identifier-free conceptual set, on WSL and on the M5 Pro. In the other direction, run SocratiCode 1.15.0 with Nemotron on a pinned subset of semble's public benchmark. Adopt as a replacement or Mac default if it matches or beats SocratiCode's 0.857/0.721 on the sealed sets with lower index time, RSS and restore cost. Refute if its public-bench lead does not carry over to the sealed conceptual set. The public labels were generated by Claude Sonnet 4.6, which also judged them, and v0.6.0 corrected 11 of them.
evidence: https://github.com/MinishLab/semble/blob/main/README.md: 'runs on CPU with no API keys, GPU, or external services required'. Provides an MCP server for Claude Code and Codex, installed with `uv tool install semble`. Indexes are cached per repo in the OS cache folder and 'invalidated automatically when files change'. `semble install` adds AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md instructions and a sub-agent.

https://github.com/MinishLab/semble/blob/main/benchmarks/README.md: 1,251 queries over 63 pinned repos in 19 languages. NDCG@10: semble 0.854, CodeRankEmbed 0.839, ColGREP 0.693, BM25 0.673, ck 0.642, codebase-memory-mcp 0.630. Ablation: ranking lifts BM25 from 0.675 to 0.834 and hybrid reaches 0.854. Queries and labels were generated by Claude Sonnet 4.6, which also judged label quality. All tools ran CPU-only, and SocratiCode is not included.

new_candidates.demonstrated_gap: New to the catalog. It addresses two recorded open gaps of the winner. (a) ai-memory captures sanitized assistant excerpts capped at 2,000 bytes, and Claude prompt capture is opted out. deja instead indexes the complete native transcripts that Claude Code and Codex already write, with no capture step and no model, and redacts credentials at index time. (b) ai-memory deletion covered only current search results. `deja forget` writes tombstones so a rebuilt index cannot restore forgotten sessions. It also offers `deja handoff --to codex`. Vendor measurements on the same 470-question cleaned LongMemEval-S set, with no LLM and no embeddings: hit@5 97.4% and evidence-recall@5 91.5%; capture costs zero model tokens. Risks: lexical ranking (preference slice 43.3% hit@1); a pooled 19,195-session haystack drops to 19% hit@1; a single maintainer; OpenSSF Code-Review 0/10; no npm provenance; 858 commits in 30 days. Source transcripts stay unredacted, and `deja secrets --scrub` rewrites native transcripts, so it must stay disabled in any trial.

new_candidates.demonstrated_gap: No one has measured how well the current lane extracts attributable text. For HTML pages that serve no markdown or llms.txt, the `read` command in the pinned winner agent-browser v0.38.1 falls back to html_to_markdownish. That function strips only script, style, noscript, svg and head (cli/src/read.rs line 1045, byte-identical on main), so nav, header, footer and aside boilerplate reaches the agent, and no extraction-accuracy evidence exists for it. The other extraction path, tvly extract, is a hosted service that needs a credential, backed by only two retained single-URL extractions. Trafilatura is a local Apache-2.0 library and CLI. It outputs TXT, Markdown or JSON with title, author, date and site-name metadata that supports attribution. It has independent evidence: WCXB held-out F1 0.841 (second of seven; dev F1 0.888 on documentation pages) against Readability at 0.736, and Bevendorff et al. 2023 named it the best single tool by mean ROUGE-LSum F1. new_candidates.demonstrated_gap: Headroom is this layer's reversible tool-output compressor, but no evidence shows it lowers provider cost. Its benefit in this stack's real sessions is not established. The only independent billed-cost study found (arXiv 2607.12161, 712 runs per arm) measured the Headroom v0.27.0 API-boundary proxy at +48.4% billed cost [+42.3, +55.0], a cost-per-success ratio of 1.464. RTK only rewrites Bash output: JetBrains measured it touching about 20% of tool-result characters, and it bypasses Read, Grep and MCP results. Caveman's local proxy compresses tool-call output (logs, JSON, CSV, diffs, test output) and keeps a byte-exact original in local SQLite behind one recovery handle. Its pinned paired suite (Claude Code 2.1.223, claude-sonnet-5, 54 runs, exact JSON oracle, recovery calls counted) reports 18/18 correct at -33.2% provider input tokens (CI 14.6% to 48.5%). The same suite reports Headroom 0.33.0 at 15/18 correct and -6.7% (CI -0.7% to 17.9%). Flags: (1) The evidence is written by a competitor, the raw harness and artifacts are unpublished, and the suite adds cache buckets together without weighting them by price. (2) The proxy runtime is BSL-1.1. Its Additional Use Grant allows self-hosted first-party use, and it converts to Apache-2.0 on 2030-06-21. (3) The CLI sends anonymous telemetry by default; `caveman telemetry off` disables it. (4) The skill alone is an output-side change that JetBrains measured independently at only -8.5% output tokens.
new_candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: A bounded workstation trial with Caveman telemetry and the Headroom beacon off, using one Claude Code build and one model. Arms: direct, headroom 0.39.0 (proxy wrap and the MCP path in use), and caveman 2.7.0 wrap. Tasks: frozen fixtures (log, JSON, CSV, test output, YAML, HTML, each with an exact oracle) plus two repository tasks with tests, at least 3 rotated repetitions per arm. Primary metric: price-weighted billed cost per successful task, with cache creation and cache read reported separately. Secondary metrics: exact-answer pass rate, turns, recovery calls and successful byte-exact recovery. Caveman replaces or complements Headroom only if its cost per success is lower with a CI that excludes zero and its pass rate does not drop. It is rejected if cost per success rises or any oracle check regresses.

new_candidates.demonstrated_gap: New to this layer. Absurd has the lowest operating cost of any durable option surveyed. Its concepts doc specifies exactly the cases this layer tests: a claim expires when a worker crashes and another worker on any host that shares the database resumes the task, completed steps are persisted and never re-executed, idempotency keys are supported, and cancellation from the API or CLI is detected at the next checkpoint or heartbeat. DBOS was refuted because its cross-host recovery needs Conductor. Here, recovery is plain claim expiry. It is rejected if a 1.0-track release or maintenance activity does not continue, or if claim expiry causes a duplicate external effect.

new_candidates.source: landscape-sweep-20260926: Coordinator follow-up search direction. Verified with GitHub GraphQL (metadata, README, docs, release notes), GitHub search ('nvidia gpu prometheus exporter', pushed after 2026-08-26), NVIDIA docs and read-only local nvidia-smi probes on both sides of WSL.
new_candidates.demonstrated_gap: The adopted pipeline has no accelerator series at all. origin/main (20b52a5b) has zero references to dcgm, nvidia_gpu_exporter, macmon, mactop, all-smi, windows_exporter or process-exporter. The adopted Collector's host_metrics receiver scrapes only cpu, memory, load and filesystem, and collector-contrib has no GPU or NVIDIA receiver at HEAD. The 2026-09-26 local-inference plan admits and guards arms on whole-device memory.free from ad-hoc 1 Hz nvidia-smi shell samples that stay outside the pipeline (plan.json L18, L449, L482). vLLM's /metrics is engine-level only. So VRAM, power, temperature and clock history cannot be reconciled with engine and native counters in the one privacy-filtered pipeline. This exporter targets GeForce-class GPUs and reads the same nvidia-smi the plan already calls (/usr/lib/wsl/lib/nvidia-smi). It also has an experimental NVML backend on Linux. It bounds collection with --collect.timeout and a background mode, and it reports failed collections explicitly. Since v1.15.0 it ships cosign-signed checksums, signed tags and build-provenance attestations. Scope correction from read-only local probes on this workstation (driver 616.64, RTX 4090): inside WSL, device-level utilization, power, temperature, SM clock and memory all answer and match the Windows-side WDDM view. Per-process memory is N/A on both sides. So a Windows-host deployment adds nothing here, and the trial belongs inside WSL.
new_candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Bounded WSL trial. Run v1.15.1 as a systemd --user unit on 127.0.0.1:9835 with per-process collection off. Drop the uuid, serial and pci labels at scrape. Scrape it with the adopted Prometheus during one production arm window, next to the plan's own window.sh 1 Hz samples, with the guard left on window.sh. Adopt only if all of these hold: (a) paired memory.free/used values agree within 1 MiB for at least 99% of pairs; (b) failed collections appear as a failure series, not as healthy-looking gaps; (c) under a known load, utilization.gpu stays within 5 percentage points of Windows-side nvidia-smi.exe read through interop; (d) the exporter's background nvidia-smi polling does not raise window.sh query latency or cause guard timeouts; (e) at least one cross-signal query works that the ad-hoc files cannot answer, such as vLLM kv_cache_usage_perc against device memory.used. Overturn if values disagree, if it only duplicates window.sh capture, or if WSL utilization diverges under load, which would confirm NVIDIA's documented limitation for that field. Test the NVML backend separately; if it fails under WSL where the nvidia-smi backend works, keep the nvidia-smi backend.

new_candidates.source: landscape-sweep-20260926: Coordinator follow-up search direction. It was the top maintained result of a GitHub repository search for 'apple silicon prometheus'. Verified with GitHub GraphQL (README and the last six release notes).
new_candidates.demonstrated_gap: The M5 Pro hosts (24 GB and 64 GB) have no accelerator, power or thermal telemetry, and every winner's macOS platform status is 'untested'. The Collector's host_metrics receiver gives CPU, memory, load and filesystem only. It has no GPU active residency, GPU/ANE power or thermal data, which an optional Metal-class model route on a Mac (such as the catalogued llama.cpp alternative) would need to qualify. On unified memory, RAM/swap pressure is the admission signal. Since v0.7.0 macmon serves Prometheus /metrics and /json without sudo and installs a per-user launchd agent. v0.8.0 added --host so the listener can be bound to loopback. It was the top maintained result in a GitHub search for Apple Silicon Prometheus exporters. Breakage risk is concrete: it reads a private macOS API. v0.7.0 had to fix a crash on Apple M5 Max caused by renumbered voltage-state keys, plus M5 core-label parsing, and v0.8.2 fixed an M3 Ultra per-core regression.
new_candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Bounded trial on the 64 GB M5 Pro. Run 'macmon serve --host 127.0.0.1' on a port other than 9090 (its default collides with Prometheus) as a launchd agent for 24 h, scraped by a local Prometheus or the Collector's prometheus receiver. Adopt only if all of these hold: (a) all series stay present with sampling overhead under 1% CPU; (b) RAM and swap agree with the Collector host_metrics memory scraper within 2%; (c) GPU active residency and power follow a known Metal load, such as a short llama.cpp Metal run; (d) where an operator can run Apple's powermetrics with sudo, they agree with it within 10%, otherwise mark that agreement as unverified; (e) the agent survives a reboot or a macOS point update. Overturn if values read zero or bogus on M5 Pro or the agent crashes. Also overturn if all-smi api or metaspartan/mactop -p passes the same checks with broader coverage or fewer components across both host classes.
evidence: https://github.com/vladkens/macmon : README says 'sudoless performance monitor' that reads data 'through a private macOS API — the same data powermetrics exposes'. The serve subcommand has GET /metrics (Prometheus) and GET /json. Default port 9090. '--host 127.0.0.1 # listen on localhost only'. serve --install creates a launchd agent in ~/Library/LaunchAgents.

https://github.com/vladkens/macmon/releases/tag/v0.7.0 : 2026-04-01. Added the HTTP server with JSON and Prometheus endpoints and launchd install. 'Fixed crash on Apple M5 Max due to renumbered voltage-states keys' and M5 E/P/S core-label parsing.

https://github.com/vladkens/macmon/releases/tag/v0.8.0 : 2026-07-24. Added --host for the metrics server and launchd service, CPU and GPU active-residency ratios, and fan metrics. Narrowed the Rust library API (breaking).
https://github.com/vladkens/macmon/releases/tag/v0.8.2 : latest release, 2026-08-04. Fixed a regression that dropped per-core CPU metrics on M3 Ultra.

new_candidates.demonstrated_gap: Neither host class has a supported path. NVIDIA's DCGM getting-started page lists supported environments as 'Bare metal and virtualized (full passthrough only)' on named Linux distributions. It says 'limited DCGM functionality is available on non-datacenter GPUs' such as GeForce, and it does not mention WSL or Windows. WSL2 reaches the GPU through the Windows driver's paravirtualization, not full passthrough. Only then compare it with the nvidia_gpu_exporter trial on field coverage and overhead.

new_candidates.source: landscape-sweep-20260926: search-first survey for a single exporter covering NVIDIA and Apple Silicon. Verified with GitHub GraphQL (metadata and README).
new_candidates.demonstrated_gap: One Apache-2.0 exporter covers both hardware classes. It reads NVIDIA GPUs through NVML, with nvidia-smi as fallback, on Linux and Windows. It reads Apple Silicon through IOReport, SMC and thermal-state readers that need no sudo under a launchd agent. It has a Prometheus API mode, opt-in per-process series, a hardened systemd unit, notarized macOS and Authenticode-signed Windows binaries, and frequent releases up to v0.26.3 (2026-09-01). If it matched both, it could replace the pair of per-platform tools proposed here (nvidia_gpu_exporter plus macmon). Unresolved gaps for that use: (1) the README never mentions WSL; (2) Linux per-process attribution reads DRM fdinfo (/proc/<pid>/fdinfo), which WSL's /dev/dxg GPU path probably does not provide (untested); (3) the Windows service runs as LocalSystem; (4) the local TUI still needs sudo on macOS; (5) the default API port 9090 collides with Prometheus. Its feature surface (remote view, replay, energy WAL) is also much larger than a single-purpose exporter's.
new_candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Run 'all-smi api' (loopback, processes=false, port other than 9090) in the same trial windows as nvidia_gpu_exporter in WSL and macmon on the M5 Pro. Prefer it over the pair only if it matches their field coverage and paired-sample agreement at equal or lower overhead, with no sudo on either host. Tolerances: NVIDIA memory within 1 MiB of window.sh; RAM, GPU residency and power within macmon's trial tolerances. Otherwise keep the per-platform tools.
evidence: https://github.com/lablup/all-smi : README says it is a cross-platform alternative to nvidia-smi for NVIDIA, AMD, Jetson and Apple Silicon. 'all-smi api --port 9090'. The [api] processes option defaults to false. Apple Silicon metrics under launchd 'need no GUI session and no sudo'. A Windows Service Control Manager service runs as LocalSystem. Linux per-process memory comes from /proc/<pid>/fdinfo. Local mode requires sudo on macOS. Release binaries are notarized (macOS) and Authenticode-signed (Windows).
https://github.com/lablup/all-smi/releases/tag/v0.26.3 : latest release, 2026-09-01. Releases v0.26.1 to v0.26.3 came out between 2026-08-24 and 2026-09-01.

new_candidates.source: landscape-sweep-20260926: search-first follow-up to the WDDM per-process finding: the maintained Windows host exporter with a vendor-neutral GPU collector. Verified with GitHub GraphQL (docs at HEAD and at the v0.31.8 tag, release notes).
new_candidates.demonstrated_gap: NVML cannot say which Windows processes hold VRAM. On this workstation, Windows nvidia-smi.exe (WDDM) lists 18 C+G processes, all with used memory N/A, and none named vmmem, vmwp or WSL. NVIDIA documents that per-process used memory is unavailable in WDDM mode. So the WSL admission guard sees only whole-device memory.free, and the plan itself records 'shared-device observation, not per-process attribution'. windows_exporter's gpu collector (present in v0.31.8, off by default) reads the Windows GPU Engine, GPU Adapter and GPU Process performance counters. It exports per-process dedicated, shared, local and committed memory and per-engine running time by Windows PID. It is the only researched path that can name non-WSL VRAM consumers. This is a diagnostic gap, not an admission gap, and closing it needs a Windows service and a cross-boundary scrape, which is a Windows-host scope decision.
new_candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Trigger: the free-VRAM guard refuses or stops an arm with no WSL-side cause. Then install v0.31.8 on the Windows host with only the gpu collector enabled, scraped from WSL over mirrored-networking loopback or a host-only firewall rule, for one week. Adopt only if per-process dedicated memory, plus whatever is left over for WSL, reconciles with nvidia-smi whole-device memory.used within 5% and names the consumer behind at least one guard event. Overturn if the counters do not reconcile, the WSL VM's share stays unattributed and unbounded, or non-WSL usage never approaches the 3,072 MiB reserve. In that last case the service and open port add risk without answering anything.
evidence: https://github.com/prometheus-community/windows_exporter/blob/v0.31.8/docs/collector.gpu.md : Perflib counters (GPU Engine, GPU Adapter, GPU Process). 'Enabled by default? No'. Series windows_gpu_process_memory_dedicated_bytes and windows_gpu_engine_time_seconds carry a process_id label.

new_candidates.demonstrated_gap: Lifecycle half of the bridge verb. The layer's open gap lists mcporter's persistence, restart, cleanup and recovery stages as not_established, and its one recorded recovery as manual (restart-receipt.json, automatic_recovery false). recipes/README.md line 201 tells operators not to restart the per-user daemon without checking other users' calls. mcporter's current docs make manual recovery a design choice: 'An unexpected daemon-process exit leaves metadata that blocks automatic replacement: an operator must verify its transports have retired before clearing stale state.' It does automatically retire and reconnect after a definitive transport close, and never replays timeouts. mcpc makes the opposite choice at the same protocol level (2026-07-28 since v0.6.0). It runs one named bridge process per session that pings the server and 'auto-reconnects on network failures or its own crashes (10s cooldown on failed retries)'. It also offers a per-session restart that touches only that session, a file-locked ~/.mcpc/sessions.json, and `mcpc clean` for orphaned processes and expired sessions. Whether its automatic recovery is also safe is untested: no overlapping server children, and no replayed uncertain calls.
new_candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Hosts: linux-wsl2-x86_64 and one macos-arm64 host. Drive the same stdio server (for example codebase-memory) and the loopback HTTP ai-memory endpoint two ways: through mcporter 0.14.1 in an owned MCPORTER_DAEMON_DIR namespace, and through mcpc 0.7.0 sessions (x402 never initialized, no --proxy). Fault matrix, 20 runs each: SIGKILL the server child, SIGKILL the mcporter daemon or mcpc bridge, and drop then restore the HTTP endpoint. Measure: (1) next call succeeds with no operator action; (2) time to first success; (3) overlapping server processes (ps before and after); (4) replayed non-idempotent calls (a counter tool); (5) residue after close/clean (processes, sockets, state files); (6) o200k token size of the tool-list JSON. Adopt mcpc for keep-alive sessions only if it recovers automatically in at least 19/20 runs per fault with zero overlapping children and zero replays. Otherwise mcporter stays: if mcpc overlaps or replays, or if mcporter in an owned namespace recovers as well.

new_candidates.source: landscape-sweep-20260926: search-first survey of maintained snapshot/time-travel stores; DuckDB is a known repository, DuckLake was not listed in this layer; confirmed by web search and ducklake.select docs
new_candidates.demonstrated_gap: DVC, the current winner, versions whole files by content hash. It cannot query an earlier snapshot in place, list the row-level inserts, updates and deletes between two snapshots, or keep a pre-correction value queryable next to the corrected one without a checkout. DuckLake v1.0 (spec and extension released 2026-04-13, shipped in DuckDB v1.5.2; DuckDB v1.5.5 is current) is embedded and local-first. It stores data as Parquet files with a DuckDB, SQLite or PostgreSQL catalog. It supports time travel by snapshot id or timestamp and has a table_changes change feed, and the project claims guaranteed backward compatibility. DuckDB is already in the stack, so no server or new credentials are needed on either host. It answers the open gap on correction retention and snapshot restoration, which DVC does not measure. It can replace DVC for tabular snapshots, or pair with it: DVC can hash-pin the catalog and Parquet files, which matters because DuckLake snapshot ids are sequence numbers, not content hashes.
new_candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Use the identity-readiness fixture: symbol-to-asset mapping plus a bar sample containing a delisting, a ticker reuse and a split. new_candidates.demonstrated_gap: The pandera open gap names correct corporate actions and a production bars/universe ingest. Those checks span interdependent frames: bars against as-of universe membership and against corporate-action records. Dataframely documents declarative constraints across collections of interdependent data frames. Pandera has no built-in cross-frame construct; its feature request #1840 for a validate() context, cited for foreign-key-like validation, has been open since 2024-10-25. The current gate (promotion_gate.py) also carries custom glue for pandera failure cases: rows with a null index, pandera's own not_nullable identifier falling into unmapped_failures, and duplicate failure rows. Dataframely reports failures per named rule (FailureInfo counts and co-occurrence), which may remove part of that glue. Not a gap: soft filtering (pandera has had drop_invalid_rows since 0.16.0) and schema-driven synthetic data (pandera[strategies] covers the pandas gate).
new_candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Run in an isolated uv venv on linux-wsl2-x86_64 and macos-arm64, with dataframely pinned exactly (v3.1.2; v3.0.0 had breaking changes). (3) A 3-frame fixture (bars, universe, splits) with injected referential and corporate-action defects must be detected by the Collection and then compared with the equivalent hand-written pandera code. (4) Wall time and peak RSS on 10M rows. Pandera stays the winner if dataframely misses parity on any fixture, needs equal or more custom code, or needs per-element Python for the exchange_calendars session check. new_candidates.demonstrated_gap: The retained broad-universe study (4,577,640 scored decisions, 45,406,248 events, 71 s) tested 5 predeclared signals x 3 horizons one at a time, and all 15 cells came back not_established. No multi-signal learned model has been run under that frozen chronology, and neither winner provides one: skfolio covers portfolio optimisation and WalkForward, EdgarTools covers filings. LightGBM survived the 2026-09-23 sweep only as a single learner. AutoGluon 1.6.x is a maintained reference AutoML baseline. 1.6.0 added `validation_structure` (time_on/group_time_on, temporal_forward_only), so internal splits respect time order. It added an `extreme` preset whose release notes say every model in it is free for commercial use; TabPFN-3 is confined to a separate `noncommercial` preset. It also exposes Chronos2Model and Toto2Model in TimeSeriesPredictor, which gives one harness for the forecasting comparison below. Two limits were verified in v1.6.3 source. First, ValidationStructure has no purge, embargo or gap parameter, and its default temporal mode is leave-one-block-out, so folds train on later blocks. Internal validation therefore cannot be trusted with overlapping H5/H20 labels, and outer splits must be external. Second, core/_setup_utils.py caps pandas <2.4.0 and pyarrow <25.0.0, while the repository pins pandas 3.0.6 and pyarrow 25.0.1, so AutoGluon needs its own environment. Governance changed in 1.6.0: maintainers now span Amazon and Prior Labs, the maker of TabPFN.
new_candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Offline run with no refetch, in an isolated venv (Python 3.13, pandas 2.3.x, extreme preset only, never noncommercial). Fit TabularPredictor on the frozen broad-universe feature panel inside the same skfolio WalkForward outer folds, with purged_size at least the label horizon (20 sessions for H20) plus an embargo. Use either num_bag_folds=0 with an explicit tuning_data block that ends before the purge, or validation_structure={'time_on': <date>, 'temporal_forward_only': True} with stacking off. Score out-of-sample rank IC and cost-adjusted top-minus-bottom decile returns per horizon against a default LightGBM and a ridge baseline on identical folds, with a date-clustered block bootstrap. Add a label-permutation placebo, whose IC must be indistinguishable from zero, and a deliberately injected one-session look-ahead feature, which the chronology audit must flag. Adopt only if AutoGluon beats LightGBM by a preregistered margin with the CI excluding zero and passes both canaries on linux-wsl2. No margin, or any canary failure, relabels it not_adopted, and LightGBM stays the learned baseline.

new_candidates.demonstrated_gap: The layer's only recorded model exclusion is Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, marked resource_infeasible in plan.json. That verdict compared whole-file size (UD-IQ4_XS, 93.7 GB) with 77.6 GB of available WSL memory. It missed two verified facts. First, the installed runtime llama.cpp b11146 already documents -lzm/--lazy-mode. Its default 'auto' reads the rows of tensors larger than 4 GiB, such as per-layer embeddings, from disk on demand. The same build also has -ncmoe/--n-cpu-moe. Second, about 28.8 GB of each Flash-Next GGUF is the 51B-parameter per_layer_token_embd n-gram table, and Qwen says that table 'can be offloaded to host memory'. In this repository only shard 1 must be resident: Q2_0 needs 37.6 GB, IQ2_XS 39.2 GB and IQ3_XXS 47.0 GB (44,861 MiB). IQ3_XXS therefore fits within 74,027 MiB of RAM plus about 14 GiB of free VRAM with production stopped. That is planning arithmetic, not a measurement. The quantizer self-reports IQ3_XXS at a 92.57 task average against 93.12 for BF16 (AIME25, GPQA-D and LCB v6 at xhigh reasoning). Qwen's own table puts Flash-Next BF16 above Qwen3.8-27B on the coding rows. No Flash-Next arm below 4 bits, and no hybrid-offload arm, has ever been measured against C0. Flags: the card YAML says apache-2.0, but its License section says the weights inherit the base model's license (qwen-community-1.0, custom). The card also warns that degradation can be larger below xhigh reasoning, and the frozen task disables thinking.
new_candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Run a bounded window on the workstation with the installed llama.cpp b11146, so no new runtime is needed. Serve IQ3_XXS, and Q2_0 as a speed arm (it adds only its 37.6 GB shard 1). Use -lm mmap --lazy-mode on, -ngl 99 and --n-cpu-moe N, with N chosen from the free VRAM measured at the window. Run the frozen sec-8k-item-extraction-20200302 set: 360 accessions with the same prompt, sampling and enable_thinking=false. Record item-code exact-set accuracy and micro-F1 with bootstrap CIs, plus prompt and decode tok/s, peak RSS, VRAM, major page faults and wall time, all against C0 (unsloth Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q4_K_M). Promote it to a heavy research-worker arm only if its F1 beats C0 beyond the CI at acceptable wall time without tripping the memory guard. If it fails to load, trips the guard, pages continuously, or ties or loses to C0, keep the exclusion, now with a measured reason.

new_candidates.demonstrated_gap: The requirement is exact event counts in the metric store, and the winner path misses them. The 2026-09-23 executed comparison ran count connector -> delta_to_cumulative -> prometheusremotewrite -> Prometheus 3.14.0. It undercounted 298/300 log records in round 8 and 16/20 intents in round 6. Collector self-telemetry recorded no drop, the root cause was not isolated, and LogQL counts were exact. Neither winner offers an upstream fix. Contrib #46441 (delta_to_cumulative keeps only the first of several points; a 2026-09-16 report says same-timestamp points are discarded) was closed NOT_PLANNED, and its fix PR #46453 was closed unmerged. In Prometheus 3.15.0, otlp-native-delta-ingestion keeps only one sample per timestamp, and otlp-deltatocumulative loses its in-memory state on restart. VictoriaMetrics stores OTLP delta samples as-is (from v1.132.0) and sums them with sum_over_time(), so no stateful conversion is needed. A raw first delta may also address the recorded 'missing initial samples' limitation; that is untested. Caveat: the vendor still recommends cumulative export. It ships as a single static Apache-2.0 binary for linux-amd64 and darwin-arm64, so a loopback-only trial runs on both hosts without credentials.
new_candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Replay the round-8 paper-sim and Dagu-arm fixtures in new prefixes. One disposable collector sends the count-connector series two ways: raw OTLP deltas to VictoriaMetrics v1.152.0 (dedup and downsampling off), and the current path to Prometheus 3.15.0. Add an injected batch of same-timestamp and reverse-ordered delta points. VictoriaMetrics passes only if sum_over_time equals the step-log MARK count (300) and intent count (20) at three points: before the kill, after a kill -9 of the collector or backend, and from a restic-restored copy. Layer checks (a)-(e) must also pass unchanged. Reject it if any count is missed, or if LogQL-derived counters (already exact) pass the same checks without a new component. Replace Prometheus only where VictoriaMetrics is exact and Prometheus is not.

new_candidates.source: landscape-sweep-20260926: Follow-up critic search direction (malicious-package heuristics for PyPI and npm installs). Verified with the GitHub API and the upstream README
new_candidates.demonstrated_gap: The stack has no malicious-code detection. At e3cbd246, git grep on origin/main finds 0 files referencing guarddog or malicious-packages. The winners, and osv-scanner, match only malware that has already been reported: GitHub MALWARE-classified GHSA records in the Grype pipeline, and MAL- records in OSV. A compromised but not yet reported PyPI, npm or crates.io version installed by the stack would pass. GuardDog v3.2.0 (2026-08-12) scans package source with YARA rules plus metadata heuristics. It correlates capabilities with threat indicators into a 0-10 risk score, runs inside a kernel sandbox (Landlock on Linux, Seatbelt on macOS) that is required by default, installs with uvx on both hosts, and has verify modes for requirements.txt, Cargo.lock, go.mod and GitHub Actions workflow files. It publishes no precision or recall figures; the README offers only a benchmarking harness (tests/samples). Its fit therefore has to be measured.
new_candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Bounded trial with uvx guarddog==3.2.0 and the sandbox on. Run pypi verify on the exported requirements of the pinned Nautilus rc5 venv (21 packages) and of the Alpaca runtime, crates verify on the rc5 Cargo.lock, npm scan of the stack's pinned npm tools, and GuardDog's own tests/samples as the positive control. Preregister the thresholds. Reject it if any package from the known-good pinned sets scores 7.6 or higher without a confirmed cause, or if medium-risk flags exceed the preregistered share of packages, or if positive-control recall falls below the floor. Also reject it if osv-scanner MAL- lookups plus Grype GHSA-malware matches already flag every sample GuardDog flags.

And 'inside the paired CI' treats CI overlap as equivalence, with no non-inferiority margin. Correct standing: add Codex memories and a no-memory control to #274 as native control arms (v1 or dual_write, rate gate 0, reset per item), not as a candidate memory owner.
